22	## Architecture Decisions
23	
24	### system_config Table for Admin-Controlled Config
25	**Date:** 2026-04-05
26	**Decision:** Single `system_config` table (key TEXT PK, value JSONB, updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ) for all admin-controlled configuration: feature flags, plan limits, pillar weights.
27	**Why:** Simple key/value store, RLS-protected (admin/super_admin only), single source of truth. Avoids separate tables for each config type. JSONB allows flexible schema per key.
28	**Tradeoff:** No schema validation at DB level (JSONB is schemaless) -- validation happens in the hooks.
29	**Cross-ref:** Pattern documented in `project_patterns.md` and `~/.claude/memory/projects/crobot.md`.
30	
31	### Feature Flags: DB-Backed, Not localStorage
32	**Date:** 2026-04-05
33	**Decision:** Feature flags live in `system_config` table, not localStorage.
34	**Why:** localStorage flags are not shared across sessions, devices, or users. Admin toggling a flag in localStorage only affects their browser. DB-backed flags are global and immediate.
35	**Implementation:**
36	- Admin hook (`useFeatureFlags`): reads/writes `system_config` with short staleTime (60s)
37	- App hook (`useFeatureFlag(key, defaultValue)`): reads with long staleTime (5min), never throws, returns defaultValue on error/loading
38	- On mutation: invalidate both `['admin', 'feature-flags']` AND `['feature-flags']` query keys
39	
40	### SQL Migrations as Comments in Hook Files
41	**Date:** 2026-04-05
42	**Decision:** SQL CREATE TABLE statements embedded as JSDoc comments at the top of hook files.
43	**Why:** Supabase projects without automated migration tooling need SQL docs somewhere. Keeping them next to the code that uses the table ensures they stay discoverable and up-to-date.
44	
45	### Hash-Based Teaser Scores for Guest Gate Wall
46	**Date:** 2026-04-05
47	**Decision:** Unauthenticated users see a simulated scan animation (no API calls) followed by a gate wall with a teaser score. Score is deterministic based on URL string (charCode sum % range + base = 45-72 range).
48	**Why:** Same URL always produces the same teaser score -- feels real and consistent. No API cost for unauthenticated users. Score range deliberately mediocre (45-72) to motivate signup.
49	
50	### TopBar: Linear/Vercel-Grade Design
51	**Date:** 2026-04-06
52	**Decision:** TopBar uses shadcn DropdownMenuTrigger with `asChild` pattern for custom trigger elements. Notifications dropdown with empty state. User dropdown with plan badge and role-based items.
53	**Why:** Previous TopBar had import abstraction mismatches (DropdownMenuPrimitive.Trigger from Radix mixed with shadcn DropdownMenu components) and hardcoded breadcrumb labels.

55	### Stripe to Dodo Payments Migration
56	**Date:** 2026-04-06
57	**Decision:** Completed full migration from Stripe to Dodo Payments.

63	**Commit:** `8996e2d`
64	**Why:** Previous UI was functional but not premium. Redesign brings visual quality to Linear/Vercel/Stripe tier. Consistent design tokens applied across all components.

66	### Supabase Migrations: Manual Application via SQL Editor
67	**Date:** 2026-04-06
68	**Decision:** All 4 SQL migrations (001_schema, 002_rls, 003_triggers, 004_admin_rbac) were combined into a single SQL block and executed manually in Supabase SQL Editor. Migrations had never been applied -- the project had zero public tables despite migration files existing.
69	**Why:** Lovable does not auto-apply `supabase/migrations/` files. The Supabase CLI `db push` requires local Docker setup. For remote-first Supabase projects, the SQL Editor is the fastest path. Combining migrations avoids dependency ordering issues.

14	### BUG-001: Duplicate Import SyntaxError (Koda)
15	**Date:** 2026-04-05
16	**Severity:** Critical (blank screen crash)

18	**What happened:** Koda appended `import { ChevronRight } from "lucide-react"` at the bottom of the file while the same import already existed at the top. Caused SyntaxError -- duplicate identifier -- app crashed with blank screen.
19	**Root cause:** Koda loses track of existing imports when making many edits to the same file in a single session. Instead of merging into the existing import block, it appends a new import statement at the end of the file.
20	**Fix:** Removed the duplicate import line. Commit: `bfc86c8`.

26	### BUG-002: Empty String SelectItem Crash (Radix UI)
27	**Date:** 2026-04-05
28	**Severity:** Critical (runtime crash)
29	**Files:** `src/pages/admin/Users.tsx`, `src/pages/admin/Scans.tsx`, `src/pages/admin/AuditLog.tsx`
30	**What happened:** `<SelectItem value="">` passed to Radix UI Select component for "All" filter options. Radix forbids empty string as SelectItem value -- crashes at runtime with TypeError.
31	**Root cause:** Radix UI internally uses the value for DOM operations requiring non-empty strings. This is a known Radix constraint but not obvious to agents.
32	**Fix:** Used `"all"` as sentinel value, mapped back to empty string in `onValueChange`:
33	```tsx
34	<Select value={filter || "all"} onValueChange={(v) => setFilter(v === "all" ? "" : v)}>
35	  <SelectItem value="all">All items</SelectItem>
36	```
37	**Commits:** `5ed9b29` (Users), `1f35ddb` (Scans + AuditLog)
38	**Prevention:** Never use empty string for Radix UI SelectItem values. Always use a non-empty sentinel like `"all"`.

The agent was likely thinking of a brand/logo icon concept but used a non-existent component name instead of picking from the lucide-react icon set.

Validation happens in hooks, not at DB level. 16 **SQL:** 17 ```sql 18 CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS system_config ( 19 key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, 20 value JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', 21 updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW() 22 ); 23 ALTER TABLE system_config ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; 24 CREATE POLICY "Admins can manage system_config" ON system_config 25 FOR ALL USING ( 26 EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM profiles WHERE id = auth.uid() AND role IN ('admin', 'super_admin')) 27 ); 28 ``` 29 **Relationships:** Prevents: localStorage feature flags antipattern. Related: useFeatureFlag hook pattern (below). 30 **Source:** ConvertScan (CROBOT), 2026-04-05 31 **Usage Metric:** 3 (feature flags, plan limits, pillar weights) 32 **Knowledge Version:** v1 33 34 --- 35 36 ### useFeatureFlag(key, defaultValue) -- Silent Fallback Hook 37 **Context:** Any React component that needs to check a feature flag without breaking if the table doesn't exist yet. 38 **Pattern:** `useFeatureFlag(key: string, defaultValue = true): boolean` -- reads from `system_config` via React Query with 5-minute staleTime. Never throws. Returns defaultValue while loading or on error. 39 **Why:** Feature flags must never break the app. During development (before table exists), during loading, or on network error, the app should work with sensible defaults. Silent fallback means flags are opt-in, not opt-out. 40 **Implementation:** 41 ```tsx 42 export function useFeatureFlag(key: string, defaultValue = true): boolean { 43 const { data } = useQuery({ 44 queryKey: ["feature-flags"], 45 queryFn: fetchAllFeatureFlags, 46 staleTime: 5 * 60 * 1000, // 5 min 47 retry: 1, 48 }); 49 if (data === undefined) { 50 const flagDef = FLAG_DEFINITIONS.find((f) => f.key === key); 51 return flagDef?.defaultValue ?? defaultValue; 52 } 53 return data[key] ?? defaultValue; 54 } 55 ``` 56 **Key design decisions:** 57 - Fetches ALL flags in one query (not one per flag) -- single network request 58 - 5-minute staleTime for app-level consumers (flags change rarely) 59 - 60-second staleTime for admin-level consumers (need faster updates) 60 - On mutation: invalidate BOTH `['admin', 'feature-flags']` AND `['feature-flags']` query keys 61 **Relationships:** Depends on: system_config table pattern (above). Works for most domains. Fallback handles domains without favicons or blocked Google requests. 96 **Source:** ConvertScan (CROBOT), 2026-04-05 97 **Usage Metric:** 1 98 **Knowledge Version:** v1 99 100 --- 101 102 ### Bulk Operations with Single Audit Log Entry 103 **Context:** Admin performing bulk actions (change plan, reset scans) on multiple users. 104 **Pattern:** 105 ```tsx 106 const results = await Promise.all( 107 userIds.map((uid) => supabase.from("profiles").update({ plan }).eq("id", uid)) 108 ); 109 // ONE audit log entry, not one per user 110 await writeAuditLog(adminId, "bulk_change_plan", "profiles", "bulk", { 111 user_ids: userIds, 112 count: userIds.length, 113 new_plan: plan, 114 }); 115 ``` 116 **Why:** Looping audit logs per user creates noise and slows down bulk operations. ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, CREATE POLICY) 193 3. Triggers (CREATE FUNCTION ... RETURNS TRIGGER, CREATE TRIGGER) 194 4. 93	### Bulk Operations Pattern
94	```

97	3. Confirmation dialog before executing
98	4. Promise.all() for per-user updates
99	5. ONE audit log entry with metadata: { user_ids: string[], count: number }

7	## Current State: Dodo Payments (fully migrated)
8	
9	CROBOT uses Dodo Payments (dodopayments.com) for all billing. The Stripe-to-Dodo migration was completed on 2026-04-06.
10	
11	**Why:** Yash uses Dodo Payments across all Boldteq SaaS products. Consistent billing provider across the portfolio.

13	---
14	
15	## Dodo Payments Integration Architecture
16	
17	### Edge Functions (Supabase Deno Runtime)
18	
19	| Function | Purpose | API Endpoint |
20	|----------|---------|-------------|
21	| `dodo-checkout` | Create subscription with hosted checkout | `POST /subscriptions` with `payment_link: true` |
22	| `dodo-webhook` | Process subscription lifecycle events | Receives standardwebhooks-signed payloads |
23	| `dodo-portal` | Fetch customer self-service portal URL | `GET /customers/{id}/portal` |
24	
25	### Dodo Payments API Reference
26	
27	**Base URL:** `https://api.dodopayments.com`
28	**Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer {DODO_API_KEY}`
29	
30	**Create Subscription (checkout):**
31	```typescript
32	// POST https://api.dodopayments.com/subscriptions
33	{
34	  billing: { currency: "USD", interval: "month" | "year", interval_count: 1 },
35	  customer: {
36	    create_new_customer: false, customer_id: "cus_xxx"
37	    // OR: create_new_customer: true, email: "...", name: "..."
38	  },
39	  product_id: "prod_xxx",
40	  payment_link: true,        // <-- returns hosted checkout URL instead of embedded form
41	  return_url: "https://app.example.com/dashboard?checkout=success",
42	  metadata: { user_id: "uuid", plan: "pro" }
43	}
44	// Response: { payment_link: string, customer_id: string, subscription_id: string }
45	```
46	
47	**Customer Portal:**
48	```typescript
49	// GET https://api.dodopayments.com/customers/{customer_id}/portal
50	// Response: { link: string }
51	```
52	
53	### Webhook Verification (standardwebhooks)
54	
55	Dodo Payments uses the `standardwebhooks` spec, NOT a proprietary verifier like Stripe.
56	
57	```typescript
58	import { Webhook } from "https://esm.sh/standardwebhooks@1.0.0";
59	
60	const wh = new Webhook(webhookSecret);  // webhookSecret = base64-encoded HMAC key (whsec_xxx)
61	const headers = {
62	  "webhook-id": req.headers.get("webhook-id"),
63	  "webhook-timestamp": req.headers.get("webhook-timestamp"),
64	  "webhook-signature": req.headers.get("webhook-signature"),
65	};
66	const event = wh.verify(body, headers);  // throws on invalid signature
67	```
68	
69	### Webhook Events Handled
70	
71	| Event | Action |
72	|-------|--------|
73	| `subscription.active` | Activate plan, set scan_limit + billing_cycle_end, persist customer_id + subscription_id |
74	| `subscription.renewed` | Update billing_cycle_end for next period |
75	| `subscription.cancelled` | Downgrade to free plan, clear subscription data, reset scan_limit to 3 |
76	| `subscription.on_hold` | Log only (future: dunning email) |
77	| `payment.failed` | Log only (future: dunning email) |
78	| `subscription.charge_failed` | Log only (future: dunning email) |
79	
80	### Database Schema (profiles table -- billing columns)
81	
82	```sql
83	dodo_customer_id TEXT        -- Dodo customer ID (cus_xxx), set on first checkout
84	dodo_subscription_id TEXT    -- Dodo subscription ID, set on subscription.active webhook
85	plan TEXT DEFAULT 'free'     -- 'free' | 'pro' | 'agency'
86	scan_limit INT DEFAULT 3    -- per billing cycle
87	billing_cycle_end TIMESTAMPTZ -- when current billing period ends
88	```
89	
90	### Frontend Hook (use-billing.ts)
91	
92	- `useCheckout({ plan, billingCycle })` -- calls `dodo-checkout` edge function, redirects to `payment_link` URL
93	- `useCustomerPortal()` -- calls `dodo-portal` edge function, redirects to portal URL
94	- `useUsage()` -- reads from AuthContext profile (no network call), returns scansUsed/scanLimit/usagePercent/plan

96	### Env Vars (Supabase Edge Function Secrets)
97	
98	| Var | Description |
99	|-----|-------------|
100	| `DODO_API_KEY` | API key from Dodo dashboard (server-side only) |
101	| `DODO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Webhook signing secret (standardwebhooks format: `whsec_xxx`) |
102	| `DODO_PRODUCT_PRO_MONTHLY` | Product ID for Pro plan monthly |
103	| `DODO_PRODUCT_PRO_ANNUAL` | Product ID for Pro plan annual |
104	| `DODO_PRODUCT_AGENCY_MONTHLY` | Product ID for Agency plan monthly |

2	name: Known Antipatterns
3	description: Patterns that caused problems across Boldteq projects — never repeat these
4	type: feedback
5	---
6	
7	## Cross-Stack Antipatterns
8	
9	### Security
10	- **Never** trust client-sent user IDs or shop IDs — always get from authenticated session
11	- **Never** expose service role keys or secret keys to client-side code
12	- **Never** skip input validation on API endpoints — always use Zod
13	
14	### Database
15	- **Never** run `findMany` without a `where` clause on tables with >1000 rows — causes timeouts
16	- **Never** use `any` type in TypeScript — masks real type errors that become runtime bugs
17	- **Never** do database schema changes directly in dashboards for production — always use migrations
18	
19	### Performance
20	- **Never** do heavy computation in Remix loaders — they run on every navigation
21	- **Never** block page render with synchronous external API calls
22	
23	### Architecture
24	- **Never** start building without researching competitors — leads to building features nobody wants
25	- **Never** skip auth or billing on v1 "to add later" — it causes painful retrofits
26	
27	### Dependencies
28	- **Never** use `file:` or `link:` local dependencies in package.json — they break in CI/CD, Vercel, Lovable, and any environment that doesn't have the local path. Incident: `@boldteq/agents: file:../claude-hub/sdk` caused `bun install` to treat `.env` as install target and fail silently. If you need shared code, publish to npm or copy the source.
29	- **Never** reference paths outside the project root (`../`) in package.json dependencies — build environments are isolated.
30	- **Never** add dependencies to package.json without verifying they install cleanly: `bun install && bun run build` (or `npm install && npm run build`).
31	
32	### Lovable-Specific
33	- **Never** restructure a Lovable project's folder layout — Lovable's AI depends on exact paths (`src/pages/`, `src/components/`, `src/hooks/`, `src/lib/`, `src/integrations/supabase/`)
34	- **Never** use Next.js patterns in Lovable projects — no `app/` directory, no server components, no API routes. It's Vite + React SPA.
35	- **Never** manually edit `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts` — it's auto-generated. Regenerate with `npx supabase gen types typescript`.
36	- **Never** create a second Supabase client instance — import from `@/integrations/supabase/client` only.
37	
38	### Shopify-Specific
39	- **Never** use Tailwind, shadcn/ui, or custom CSS in Shopify admin apps — Polaris only. Shopify reviewers reject non-Polaris UI.
40	- **Never** use external payment providers (Dodo Payments, etc.) for Shopify app billing — Shopify Billing API only.
41	- **Never** query database without shop scope — every Prisma query needs `where: { shop: session.shop }`.
42	- **Never** skip GDPR webhooks — `customers/data_request`, `customers/redact`, `shop/redact` are mandatory even with zero stored data.
43	- **Never** add GDPR webhook topics (`customers/data_request`, `customers/redact`, `shop/redact`) to `shopify.app.toml` — they cause deploy error "The following topic is invalid". Configure them in Shopify Partner Dashboard > App Setup > Privacy instead. (Pinzo, 2026-04-03)
44	- **Never** use raw HTML elements (`<strong>`, `<em>`, `<div style>`) in Shopify admin routes — use Polaris equivalents: `<Text fontWeight="semibold">`, `<Text tone="subdued">`, `<Box minWidth="X">`. (Pinzo, 2026-04-03)
45	- **Never** skip CSS sanitization on user-provided custom CSS in widget configs — sanitize both on save (admin) and on render (storefront API). Double-sanitize prevents XSS from either vector. (Pinzo, 2026-04-03)
46	- **Never** hardcode admin-specific values (shop domains, chat widget tokens) in source code — use environment variables and `.env.example`. These leak into version control and break multi-environment deploys. (Pinzo, 2026-04-03)
47	- **Never** forget to delete ALL shop-scoped models in `shop/redact` and `app/uninstalled` webhook handlers — audit every Prisma model with a `shop` field. Missing models = GDPR compliance gap. (Pinzo, 2026-04-03)
48	- **Never** run `prisma migrate dev` when migration history is drifted on the production database — use `prisma db push` to sync schema without creating a new migration. `migrate dev` fails when drift is detected. (Pinzo, 2026-04-03)
49	
50	---
51	
52	## Agent Output Antipatterns (Crobot Incident — 2026-04)
53	
54	These patterns were discovered when agents reported "done" on the Crobot project but the app was not functional. **Every agent must verify against these before claiming completion.**
55	
56	### Redesign Agent Placeholder Components (NEW — 2026-04-06)
57	- **Never** use a component name that doesn't exist in the project or its dependencies — redesign agents sometimes invent placeholder names like `BrandIcon`, `LogoIcon`, `AppIcon` that "look right" but are not real components. The build may still pass if the undefined reference doesn't trigger a strict TypeScript error.
58	- **Never** assume an icon exists in lucide-react without checking — the library has 1400+ icons but agents still invent names that aren't in it. After a redesign: `grep -rn "BrandIcon\|PlaceholderIcon\|CustomIcon\|LogoIcon\|AppIcon" src/`
59	- **Never** skip `npm run build` after a UI redesign touching 10+ files — this is the minimum verification. Also run `npm run lint` to catch unused/undefined imports.
60	- **Root cause:** When redesign agents rewrite UI across many files in one session, they lose track of which components are real imports vs. conceptual placeholders. The agent "thinks" of a brand icon concept and writes `BrandIcon` instead of picking an actual icon like `ScanLine` from lucide-react.
61	- **Incident:** CROBOT, 2026-04-06. `BrandIcon` used in Landing.tsx (lines 124, 727) — never imported, doesn't exist. Fixed by replacing with `ScanLine`. Commit: `10f68f1`.
62	- **Prevention:** After any redesign of 10+ files, run the Post-Redesign Verification Checklist (documented in CROBOT `project_patterns.md`).
63	
64	### Supabase Migrations Not Applied (NEW — 2026-04-06)
65	- **Never** assume Supabase migrations are auto-applied in Lovable-origin projects — they are NOT. Lovable generates migration files in `supabase/migrations/` but never executes them against the Supabase project.
66	- **Never** skip database table verification after project setup — always check Supabase Dashboard > Table Editor to confirm tables exist.
67	- **Never** claim a Supabase-backed app is "architecturally complete" without verifying the database has actual tables — code-complete and database-ready are two different states.
68	- **Root cause:** No workflow step was responsible for applying migrations. The Supabase CLI `db push` requires local Docker. Lovable does not run migrations. The app builds and starts successfully with zero tables — failures are silent runtime errors.
69	- **Incident:** CROBOT, 2026-04-06. Supabase project `hyxlmmkrbipufoqkkhba` had zero public tables despite 4 migration files existing. All 4 had to be combined and run manually in SQL Editor.
70	- **Prevention:** Add "verify tables exist in Supabase Dashboard" as a mandatory step after scaffold. For Lovable projects, always manually apply migrations via SQL Editor.
71	
72	### "Done But Broken" Patterns
73	- **Never** claim a page is "built" if it returns <500 bytes of content — that's an empty page
74	- **Never** claim billing is "integrated" if the pricing page shows $0, "TBD", or placeholder prices
75	- **Never** claim admin panel is "ready" if /admin returns 404 or loads with empty tables
76	- **Never** claim auth is "working" if the login form renders but doesn't submit or create sessions
77	- **Never** claim dashboard is "complete" if it shows only empty states with no data fetching logic
78	- **Never** claim a feature is "done" based solely on the build succeeding — build ≠ functional
79	
80	### Verification Failures
81	- **Never** skip functional verification — running `npm run build` is not the same as verifying the app works
82	- **Never** report "tests pass" if the tests only check compilation, not actual feature behavior
83	- **Never** deploy without verifying that critical pages load with real content (>minimum byte thresholds)
84	- **Never** mark a sprint as complete without someone (human or agent) actually navigating to every claimed page
85	
86	### Architecture Gaps
87	- **Never** skip admin panel in architecture — every SaaS product needs user management
88	- **Never** leave pricing/billing as "to be added later" — it's a V1 requirement
89	- **Never** define pages without specifying what content/components they contain
90	- **Never** hand off architecture to Koda without a complete page/route map with component details
91	
92	### Copy/Content Gaps
93	- **Never** ship pages with "Coming Soon", "Lorem ipsum", "TODO", or "[App Name]" placeholder text
94	- **Never** leave empty states undefined — every list/table needs an empty state with a call to action
95	- **Never** ship error messages that just say "Error" — include what happened and what to do next
96	
97	### Navigation & Layout Bugs (CRITICAL — #1 Recurring Issue Across ALL Projects)
98	
99	**Full protocol:** `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/layout-navigation-consistency.md`
100

100	
101	**The core rule: EVERY authenticated page MUST be wrapped in a shared layout with sidebar + header. No exceptions.**
102	
103	- **Never** render an authenticated page without a shared layout wrapper — EVERY page needs sidebar + header. This is the SINGLE MOST COMMON bug agents produce.
104	- **Never** build a page as a standalone component without importing AppLayout/SidebarLayout — this creates "orphan pages" with no navigation
105	- **Never** create a page without ALSO adding its sidebar nav link in the SAME commit — pages without nav links are unreachable
106	- **Never** add a route to App.tsx without verifying the page component uses the layout wrapper — run `grep -rn "SidebarLayout" src/pages/NewPage.tsx` after every new page
107	- **Never** add a new admin sidebar item without adding the corresponding component to `sectionComponents` — leads to blank tab content
108	- **Never** hardcode sidebar width differently per page — use a shared layout with consistent sidebar width (w-56)
109	- **Never** forget sidebar active state — sidebar must highlight the current page/tab
110	- **Never** skip mobile sidebar testing — sidebar must collapse to drawer on mobile with a trigger button (SidebarTrigger)
111	- **Never** build Settings, Billing, or Profile pages without the same sidebar as Dashboard — these are the #1 pages where sidebar goes missing
112	- **Never** claim admin panel is "done" if any sidebar item renders blank content when clicked
113	- **Never** let sidebar links point to routes that don't exist — every sidebar item must map to a real, rendered page

116	**Mandatory post-page-creation check:**

119	echo "Routes:" && grep -c "path=" src/App.tsx
120	echo "Pages with sidebar:" && grep -rln "SidebarLayout" src/pages/ | wc -l
121	```
122	
123	### Layout Structure Anti-Patterns
124	- **Never** use `min-h-screen` without `overflow-hidden` on the flex container — causes double scrollbars
125	- **Never** put the sidebar inside individual page components — sidebar belongs in the shared layout
126	- **Never** use different header components on different pages — one AppHeader for all authenticated pages
127	- **Never** skip `overflow-y-auto` on the main content area — content must scroll independently from sidebar
128	- **Never** forget `h-svh` (or `h-screen`) on the root layout container — prevents proper full-viewport layout
129	
130	### UI/UX Micro-Bugs (Common in Agent-Built Apps — Zero Tolerance)
131	
132	**Loading & State Bugs:**
133	- **Never** show a blank area while data loads — always use Skeleton components matching final layout shape
134	- **Never** show a raw spinner (Spinner/CircularProgress) as a loading state — use Skeleton instead
135	- **Never** render a list/table without an empty state — icon + message + CTA button required
136	- **Never** show an error as just "Error" or "Something went wrong" — include what failed and a retry action
137	- **Never** leave a form without inline validation errors — red border + error text next to the field
138	
139	**Button & Form Bugs:**
140	- **Never** leave an async button without loading state — show spinner + disable during operation
141	- **Never** allow double-click on submit buttons — disable immediately on first click
142	- **Never** allow a delete/destructive action without confirmation dialog
143	- **Never** reset form fields when validation fails — preserve user input
144	- **Never** submit a form without success feedback — toast.success() with specific message
145	
146	**Feedback & Notification Bugs:**
147	- **Never** use window.alert() or window.confirm() — use sonner toast or Dialog component
148	- **Never** show a generic "Success" toast — say what succeeded ("Project saved", "User invited")
149	- **Never** show a generic "Error" toast — say what failed ("Failed to save project — please try again")
150	- **Never** complete a mutation silently — every create/update/delete needs a toast
151	
152	**Visual Consistency Bugs:**
153	- **Never** use text-gray-500, bg-blue-600, or any hardcoded color — use theme tokens (text-muted-foreground, bg-primary)
154	- **Never** mix font sizes for the same purpose — page titles always text-2xl, body always text-sm
155	- **Never** use inconsistent spacing — gap-4 between cards, space-y-4 in forms, p-6 page padding
156	- **Never** use font-bold in SaaS UI — use font-semibold for titles, font-medium for labels
157	- **Never** leave console.log in production components — remove all debug logging
158	
159	**Responsive Bugs:**
160	- **Never** use grid-cols-3 or higher without responsive breakpoints (md:grid-cols-3)
161	- **Never** use fixed pixel widths (w-[400px]) on content that should be flexible
162	- **Never** hide important functionality behind a breakpoint (must work on mobile)
163	- **Never** leave tables without horizontal scroll or card-layout fallback on mobile
164	
165	**Interaction Bugs:**
166	- **Never** use onClick on a div/span without role="button" and keyboard support
167	- **Never** leave an interactive element without a hover effect
168	- **Never** leave an input without a visible focus ring
169	- **Never** let focus escape a modal/dialog — trap focus and return on close

173	## Package Management Failures (Lovable/Vite Projects)
174	
175	**The #1 recurring issue.** App goes blank after installing a package. Full protocol: `patterns/good/lovable-package-management.md`

177	**Banned Patterns:**
178	- **Never** use `"pkg": "file:../path"` or `"pkg": "link:../path"` in package.json — breaks ALL remote builds (Lovable, Vercel, CI/CD). Incident: `"@boldteq/agents": "file:../claude-hub/sdk"` caused silent bun install failure.
179	- **Never** install packages with `--force` as a permanent fix — masks dependency conflicts that cause runtime crashes
180	- **Never** mix package managers — don't use both npm and bun. Pick one, delete the other's lock file.
181	- **Never** install 5+ packages at once — install one, verify build, then next. Can't isolate breakage otherwise.
182	- **Never** install Node.js-only packages for browser use — `fs`, `path`, `crypto` don't exist in Vite/browser
183	- **Never** skip `npm run build` after installing a package — the build catches 90% of issues
184	- **Never** blindly accept Lovable's auto-fix suggestions — often corrupts `vite.config.ts` (check `base: './'` and plugin list)

23	### system_config Table for Admin-Controlled Config
24	**Date:** 2026-04-05
25	**Decision:** Use a single `system_config` table (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value JSONB, updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ) for all admin-controlled configuration: feature flags, plan limits, pillar weights.
26	**Why:** Simple key/value store, RLS-protected (admin/super_admin only), single source of truth. Avoids separate tables for each config type. JSONB allows flexible schema per key.
27	**Tradeoff:** No schema validation at DB level (JSONB is schemaless) -- validation happens in the hooks.
28	
29	### Feature Flags: DB-Backed, Not localStorage
30	**Date:** 2026-04-05
31	**Decision:** Migrated feature flags from localStorage to `system_config` table.
32	**Why:** localStorage flags are not shared across sessions, devices, or users. Admin toggling a flag in localStorage only affects their browser. DB-backed flags are global and immediate.
33	**Implementation:** Admin hook (`useFeatureFlags`) reads/writes with short staleTime (60s). App hook (`useFeatureFlag(key, defaultValue)`) reads with long staleTime (5min), never throws, returns defaultValue on error/loading.

36	**Date:** 2026-04-05
37	**Decision:** On mutation success, invalidate both `['admin', 'feature-flags']` AND `['feature-flags']` query keys.

41	**Date:** 2026-04-05
